sentences.text: Orienantius ritteri was an extinct bird belonging to the Enantiornithes group found in China.
Its fossils were discovered within the Huajiying Formation of Hebei Province.
Scientists estimated that these individuals were roughly the same size as the modern Eurasian Skylark.
The remains preserve extensive soft tissues such as the neck, legs, wings, and internal organs, a rare find for ancient birds.
The genus was formally described by Liu and colleagues in 2019.
The specific name ritteri honors the German scientist Johann Wilhelm Ritter.
This creature lived during the Hauterivian stage, between 132.6 and 125.77 million years ago.
